310: And now, please come and curse this nation for me, etc.: Rabbi Abba began, "A prayer of the poor man when he is enwrapped, etc. (Psalms 102:1). There are three about whom it is written, "a prayer," and they fulfilled this word. One was Moses, one was David, and one was the poor man. For it was integrated by them, and it was connected to them. And if you may say, behold it is written: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet — behold there are four! However, Habakkuk was not [mentioned] because of the prayer, even though prayer was written about him. [Rather,] it is praise and thanksgiving to the Holy One, blessed be He, for His giving him life. And He had done miracles and great deeds with him, as behold, he was the son of the Shunamite.

However, these three are called prayer: A prayer of Moses, the man of God (Psalms 90:1). This is a prayer that there is none like it with other people. A prayer of David (Psalms 86:1). This is a prayer that there is none like it with other kings. A prayer of the poor man. This is a prayer from those three. Which is more important than all of them? I would say [it is] the prayer of the poor man. That prayer precedes the prayer of Moses and precedes the prayer of David, and it precedes all the other prayers in the world.

What is the reason? Because the poor man is brokenhearted. And it is written: The Lord is close to the brokenhearted, etc. (Psalms 34:19). And the poor person always has an argument with the Holy One, blessed be He; and the Holy One, blessed be He, pays attention and listens to his word. When he prays his prayer, all the windows of the firmaments open up. And that poor brokenhearted person pushes off all of the other prayers that ascend upwards. As it is written: A prayer of the poor man when he is enwrapped [ya'atof]. It should have been, "when he enwraps himself!" What is [the meaning of], "when he ya'atof?" Rather, it is [that] he makes an envelope over all the prayers of the world, and they do not ascend until his prayer has ascended.
